controlling_plan_delta.old_SME46_line: **Pages:** spatial-field-summary-estimators / spatial-field-summary-estimators-examples. **A:** Define bounded windows $W_n\subset\mathbb R^d$ with $|W_n|\to\infty$ and Van Hove boundary ratio $|(W_n+K)\setminus W_n|/|W_n|\to0$ for every compact $K$; require joint measurability and integrability for $\bar X_{W_n}=|W_n|^{-1}\int_{W_n}X(s)\,ds$. Under stationary finite-variance $X$ with absolutely integrable covariance, prove $E\bar X_{W_n}=EX(0)$ and $L^2$ consistency from the covariance double integral/boundary limit. For lattice observations, define lagged sample covariance/variogram estimators and prove only the source-backed asymptotic-unbiasedness result under consistency of the mean estimate; the covariance estimate need not be PSD. Define the regular-grid periodogram convention, derive its expected Fejer convolution, and prove smoothing bias only under the stated continuity/kernel/bandwidth conditions. No variance consistency, weak consistency or CLT. **B:** boundary-dominated window and non-PSD covariance. **Requires:** SME-45; published covariance and Bochner clauses (AC+DC for Bochner). **Sources:** Spodarev 2024 Thm.2.5, Lemmas 2.2/2.8/2.10 pp.16–20; Stanford Lecture 6 is plug-in caution, not full asymptotic proof.

Under stationary finite-variance $X$ with absolutely integrable covariance, prove $E\bar X_{W_n}=EX(0)$ and $L^2$ consistency from the covariance double integral/boundary limit. For lattice observations, define lagged sample covariance/variogram estimators and prove only the source-backed asymptotic-unbiasedness result under consistency of the mean estimate; the covariance estimate need not be PSD. Define the regular-grid periodogram convention, derive its expected Fejer convolution, and prove smoothing bias only under the stated continuity/kernel/bandwidth conditions. For fixed spacing $\delta>0$, the general target is the sampled lattice spectrum: prove the density alias identity $g_\delta(\theta)=\delta^{-d}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}f((\theta+2\pi k)/\delta)$. For the physically normalized raw and smoothed estimates $\delta^d I_n(\delta\omega_0)$ and $\delta^d\widetilde f_{n,b_n}(\delta\omega_0)$, recover the unaliased continuous-space value only under the exact zero-noncentral-alias condition, with the periodized density bounded and continuous at the target; a continuous spectrum compactly supported inside the Nyquist cube is a proved sufficient case. Explicitly refute the source's unconditional unaliased fixed-grid target. No variance consistency, weak consistency or CLT. **B:** boundary-dominated window and non-PSD covariance. **Requires:** SME-45; published covariance and Bochner clauses (AC+DC for Bochner). **Sources:** Spodarev 2024 Thm.2.5, Lemmas 2.2/2.8/2.10 pp.16–20; Stanford Lecture 6 is plug-in caution, not full asymptotic proof.

counterexample.claim_refuted: A fixed integer-grid periodogram from a continuous-space field with continuous spectral density generally has expectation converging to the unaliased continuous-space density (Spodarev Lemma2.10(b)); likewise unconditional unaliased smoothing bias.
counterexample.density_construction: Take d=1, delta=1 and a=pi/4. Define b(x)=exp(1-1/(1-(x/a)^2)) for |x|<a and b(x)=0 otherwise. It is nonnegative, even, compactly supported, has b(0)=1 and is C-infinity. Let f(omega)=b(omega-2pi)+b(omega+2pi) and M=integral_R f(omega)domega=2 integral_-a^a b(x)dx in (0,infinity). Then f is smooth, even, nonnegative, integrable, and f(0)=0.
counterexample.smoothness_verification: For s=1-(x/a)^2>0, each interior derivative of b is a finite sum of e^(1-1/s) times a polynomial in x divided by an integer power of s, by induction using the chain and product rules. Its numerator is bounded near each endpoint. For every integer r>=0, s^-r exp(-1/s) tends to0 as s downarrow0: put v=1/s and use exp(v)>=v^(r+1)/(r+1)! to bound v^r exp(-v) by (r+1)!/v. Hence all derivatives extend by0 at both endpoints. Induction and one-sided difference quotients (or integration of the extending derivative) prove the zero extension is C-infinity.
counterexample.field_realization: Let R have probability density f/M and U be independent uniform on [-pi,pi), on their finite product probability space. Define X(t)=sqrt(2M) cos(Rt+U), t in R. Its paths are continuous and the field is jointly measurable. Conditional on R, uniform phase gives E cos(Rt+U)=0 and E[cos(Rs+U)cos(Rt+U)]=(1/2)cos(R(t-s)). Consequently EX(t)=0 and Cov(X(s),X(t))=M E cos(R(t-s))=integral_R exp(i(t-s)omega) f(omega)domega, the imaginary part vanishing because f is even. All variables are bounded by sqrt(2M), so finite second moments hold. Conditional uniform phase is unchanged by U -> U+Rh modulo2pi, hence every finite-dimensional law is shift-invariant. This directly realizes the proposed spectrum without assuming an unproved Gaussian existence result.
counterexample.covariance_integrability: C(h)=integral exp(ih omega)f(omega)domega is bounded by M. For h!=0, two integrations by parts have zero boundary terms because f is smooth and compactly supported, and give |C(h)|<=||f_second_derivative||_L1/h^2. Thus C is absolutely integrable on R. The witness therefore also satisfies the continuous covariance/integrability setup preceding source Definition2.9.
counterexample.alias_and_limit: On [-pi,pi), because a<pi, only k=1 and k=-1 contribute to g_1(theta)=sum_k f(theta+2pi k); hence g_1(theta)=2b(theta), extended periodically. It is bounded and continuous on the entire torus and g_1(0)=2. The actual Fejer/point-continuity proof gives E I_n(0)->2 and, for every kernel and bandwidth satisfying the authored smoothing hypotheses, E tilde_f_n(0)->2. Both limits disagree with unaliased f(0)=0. In fact the same conflict occurs in a neighborhood of0 where b(theta)>0 and f(theta)=0, so the source a.e. qualification does not rescue its claim.
counterexample.unaliased_recovery: For a general specified nonnegative f with periodized density bounded and continuous at the target, the physically normalized expectation limit is sum_k f(omega0+2pi k/delta). It equals f(omega0) exactly when all k!=0 terms vanish. A continuous f supported compactly inside the open Nyquist cube verifies this condition and the needed density regularity, without restricting the general aliased branch.
